info.title: Vortex IQ Automations API
info.description:
REST API for Vortex IQ Automations. List the templates your organisation can use, set automations up on your
stores, schedule them, run them, and follow every run, from your own tools instead of the Automations screens.

The API is served from `https://automations-api.vortexiq.ai`; the login that gives you a token is on
`https://app.vortexiq.ai`. Every call acts as the person who logged in, within their organisation, and every
answer is JSON. See [Authentication](/automations/api/authentication).

username.description: Your name as registered on your Vortex IQ account (first name, last name, or full name; case-insensitive).

email.description: The email of your Vortex IQ user. The account must be active.

organization_name.description: Your organisation's name exactly as registered (case-insensitive). Your user must belong to this organisation.

client_id.description: Your organisation's API client id, issued by Vortex IQ. It starts with `viq_auto_`.

client_secret.description: Your organisation's API client secret. Shown once at issue time; keep it server-side.

grant_type.description: Optional. Sent by OAuth 2.0 clients; when present it must be `client_credentials`.

200.description: Authenticated. Send `access_token` as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on every call to `https://automations-api.vortexiq.ai`.

access_token.description: The bearer token (a signed JWT). Treat it as a secret.

expires_in.description: Token lifetime in seconds (3600, one hour).

scope.description: What the token may do, space-separated. A credential's token never holds `automations:approve`.

direct.description: Used by the Vortex IQ app's own screens. You can ignore it.

401.description: One of the provided values could not be validated. The answer is deliberately generic and takes the same time whichever value was wrong.

example.message: The provided username, email, organization name or API credential could not be validated.

422.description: A field is missing or malformed, or `grant_type` is not `client_credentials`.

client_secret: The client secret field is required.

429.description: More than 10 login attempts a minute from your address. Wait a minute and try again.

503.description: API access is not configured on this environment.

post.description:
Exchange your identity (username, email, organisation name) and your organisation's API credential
(`client_id` and `client_secret`) for a bearer token valid for 60 minutes. The credential is issued per
organisation by Vortex IQ: contact [support](https://www.vortexiq.ai/contact-us) to have one provisioned.

The token acts as the person you name, within their organisation, with the credential's scopes
(`automations:read automations:write`). It never approves. Everything it creates is recorded as made by that
person through the API, with the credential's client id.

Send the request as JSON, as here, or as an OAuth 2.0 client-credentials form
(`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, `grant_type=client_credentials`) with the client id and secret as HTTP
Basic authentication and `username`, `email` and `organization_name` as extra form fields, which is what
Postman's OAuth 2.0 helper sends. Values in the address are ignored: send everything in the body.

This endpoint is served by `https://app.vortexiq.ai`; every other endpoint by
`https://automations-api.vortexiq.ai`. Rate limited to 10 requests a minute.

get.description:
The templates your organisation can set up: for every platform it has a connected store or account on. Each
template says what it does, what it reads and writes, its inputs and default schedule, and whether it is ready
(`readiness.ready`). A template that needs a connection your organisation does not have yet says which in
`readiness`.

Pass a template's `id` as `template_id` when you [create an automation](/automations/api/create-automation).

Needs the `automations:read` scope.

get.description:
One template by id, with its steps, inputs, default schedule and readiness. Answers `404` when no template
has this id.

Needs the `automations:read` scope.

200.description: Your organisation's stores and accounts, connected ones first, then by name.

get.description:
What an automation can run on: your organisation's connected stores, and the accounts some templates run on
instead, such as a cloud account. Each has the `integration_id` you pass when you
[create an automation](/automations/api/create-automation), its platform, and the timezone its automations run
in unless you choose another.

Stores are connected in the Vortex IQ app (**Settings**, **Connected Sources**), never through this API.

Needs the `automations:read` scope.

Your organisation's Google Sheets and Microsoft Teams connections that a step of an
[imported workflow](/automations/api/create-workflow-automation) can send to, connected ones first. Never a key:
a Sheets connection says which spreadsheet it writes to, a Teams connection which channel.

Needs the `automations:read` scope.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Only automations in this state: `draft`, `active`, `paused` or `archived`.

parameters.name: platform
parameters.description: Only automations on this platform, such as `shopify`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Automations a page, 1 to 100 (25 unless you say).

200.description: A page of automations, newest first.

get.description:
Your organisation's automations, newest first, a page at a time. Filter with `state` and `platform`. Each
automation carries its schedule, its next run, its state, and who set it up: `created_by` (the person),
`created_via` (`ui` for the Vortex IQ app, `api-token` for this API) and `api_client_id`.

Needs the `automations:read` scope.

201.description: Created. The automation, with its first run time when it has a schedule.

post.description:
Set up an automation from a [template](/automations/api/list-templates) on one of your
[stores](/automations/api/list-stores), with the template's inputs and a schedule.

- With a schedule (`daily`, `weekly` and the other cadences), the automation is `active` and its runs are
  queued at the times the schedule gives, in the store's timezone unless you send `timezone`.
- With `schedule.cadence: manual`, it is a `draft` that runs only when you
  [run it now](/automations/api/run-now).
- A template that starts when the store sends an event (it has a `trigger`) takes only
  `schedule.cadence: manual`, and its automation is `active` at once.

The automation is set up even when the template is not ready yet (its `readiness` says why, such as a
connection your organisation does not have). Its runs then end `refused` (`connection_missing`), saying what
to connect, until that connection is there.

The automation is recorded as created by the person you logged in as, through the API (`created_via:
api-token`, with your `api_client_id`). Answers `404` when the template or the store is not your
organisation's, and `422` when the store is not connected, or an input or the schedule is not valid.

Needs the `automations:write` scope.

get.description:
One automation: its template, store, inputs, schedule and timezone, its state and next run, its failure
count, and who set it up and how. Keep its `version`: changing the automation needs it.

Needs the `automations:read` scope.

409.description: Your version is stale (`stale_version`; `data` carries the current automation), or a workflow change is not the one you previewed (`preview_mismatch`).

patch.description:
Change an automation's name, inputs, schedule or timezone. Send only what changes, with the `version` you last
read: if the automation has changed since, the answer is `409 stale_version` with the current automation, so
read it again and retry. Its coming runs are worked out again from a new schedule or timezone.

Giving a draft a schedule turns it on. For an imported workflow, `workflow` with the `preview_hash` from
[Preview workflow change](/automations/api/preview-workflow-change) replaces its steps.

Needs the `automations:write` scope.

post.description:
Stop an automation's schedule. Nothing more is queued for it until you resume it, and its scheduled runs
already queued are cancelled (`automation_off`). A run already going carries on, and so do a run started by
hand and one someone approved; you can still [run it now](/automations/api/run-now) by hand. Answers `409
wrong_state` when it is already paused or archived.

Needs the `automations:write` scope.

Start a paused automation's schedule again, or switch on a draft that starts when its store sends an event,
which has no schedule to give it. Its failure count and the reason it was paused are cleared. Answers `409
wrong_state` when it is not paused, and `422` when a step of an imported workflow still needs a connection or
cannot run, with the steps named in `errors.steps`.

Needs the `automations:write` scope.

Archive an automation: nothing more runs. Its queued runs are cancelled (`automation_off`), one someone
approved too, and it cannot be run by hand while archived. Its runs and history stay readable, and you can
[restore](/automations/api/restore-automation) it. Answers `409 wrong_state` when it is already archived.

Needs the `automations:write` scope.

Bring an archived automation back. It returns paused, so nothing runs until you
[resume](/automations/api/resume-automation) it.

Needs the `automations:write` scope.

202.description: Accepted. The run is queued; follow it with Get run.

post.description:
Queue a run of an automation now. The answer comes at once (`202`) with the run, `queued`; follow it with
[Get run](/automations/api/get-run). Running a draft switches it on (`active`).

Send an `idempotency_key` of at least 8 characters, new for each run you mean, and one across all your
organisation's automations: the same key returns the same run, so a request you retry after a timeout never
starts two runs, and a key already used for another of your automations is refused with `422`. `mode: test`
runs for real but refuses every change to your store, so you can see what a run would do.

Answers `409 wrong_state` when the automation is archived, or starts when its store sends an event (it has
no Run now), and `422` when it cannot run yet: the store, or an account it reads, is not connected, or a step
of an imported workflow needs a connection (`steps_unconfigured`) or cannot run (`step_unsupported`). The
message says what to do. A connection a template needs beside its store is checked as the run starts: without
it the run ends `refused` (`connection_missing`), saying what to connect.

Needs the `automations:write` scope.

get.description:
Run history, newest first, a page at a time. Filter by `automation_id` and `status`. Each run carries its
status, timings, summary, and who started it: `created_via` and `api_client_id` for a run started through this
API, and `trigger` (`manual`, `schedule` or `event`).

Needs the `automations:read` scope.

parameters.name: after_seq
parameters.description: Only the steps after this sequence number.

steps_available.description: False when the step history could not be read just now; `steps` is then empty, and the run's status is still current.

records.finding: Add a SKU for this variant.

coverage.scope: Online Store catalogue; online sellable quantity; default shop currency. Market-specific pricing and checkout eligibility require review in Shopify.

result.next_step: Open the linked products and review these findings before making changes.

get.description:
One run: its status, timings, summary and result, and the steps it has taken. While the run is `queued` or
`running`, ask again every few seconds; pass the highest step `seq` you already have as `after_seq` to get only
the steps since. A run ends `succeeded`, `failed`, `refused`, `cancelled` or `expired`; `waiting_approval`
means it waits for someone to decide in the Vortex IQ app.

If the step history cannot be read for a moment, the run's status still comes back, with `steps_available:
false`.

Needs the `automations:read` scope.

post.description:
Stop a run. A `queued` run is cancelled at once. A `running` run is asked to stop: it finishes as
`cancelled` at its next check-in, about 15 seconds by default, keeping what had already finished. Answers
`409 wrong_state` when the run has already ended, and when it is `waiting_approval`: a run waiting for a
decision is ended by rejecting it in the Vortex IQ app, not here.

Needs the `automations:write` scope.

200.description: The next three times the rule would run.

post.description:
The next three times a schedule would run in a timezone, before you save it. Nothing is saved. A scheduled
run starts within ten minutes after its time, so treat the times as "at about".

Cadences: `manual`, `once` (with `date` and `run_at`), `hourly`, `every_6_hours`, `daily`, `weekdays` (with
`days`, 1 is Monday), `weekly` (with `day_of_week`) and `monthly` (with `day_of_month`, or `week_of_month`
and `day_of_week`). `run_at` is `HH:MM` in the timezone.

Needs the `automations:read` scope.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: The end of the period (ISO 8601), at most 62 days after `from`.

200.description: The coming runs in the period, by the time they will really run.

get.description:
The coming runs of your automations between `from` and `to`, at most 62 days apart, as a calendar shows them:
each with its `run_at`, its state (`pending`, `queued` or `skipped`) and its `version`. Pass `automation_id`
for one automation's.

Runs further ahead are worked out from the schedule (`projected: true`): you can move one (with
`occurrence_version: 0`), and skip it once it comes closer. Past runs are in
[List runs](/automations/api/list-runs).

Needs the `automations:read` scope.

200.description: The coming run after the change, and the automation as it now is.

409.description: A version is stale (`stale_version`, with what is current) or the row was already decided (`wrong_state`).

post.description:
Move one coming run to another time. With `scope: this`, only that run moves. With `scope: this_and_later`,
the schedule itself changes (its time of day, and its weekday or day of the month) and every later run
follows; not for hourly cadences.

Send the coming run's `slot_at` and `version` from [List coming runs](/automations/api/list-occurrences)
(`0` for a projected one, which is moved the same way), and the automation's `version`. A stale version
answers `409`; a run already queued or skipped answers `409 wrong_state`, and a time in the past `422`.

Needs the `automations:write` scope.

200.description: The coming run after the change, and the automation as it now is.

409.description: The version is stale (`stale_version`, with what is current) or the row was already decided (`wrong_state`).

post.description:
Skip one coming run. It stays in the calendar marked as skipped, and the schedule carries on after it. Send
its `slot_at` and `version` from [List coming runs](/automations/api/list-occurrences). A projected coming run
(`projected: true`) cannot be skipped until it comes closer: it answers `404` until then.

Needs the `automations:write` scope.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only approvals in this status (`waiting` unless you say).

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Approvals a page, 1 to 100 (25 unless you say).

get.description:
Runs waiting for a decision, oldest first, with what each would change. Filter by `status` (`waiting` unless
you say). Approving and rejecting happen in the Vortex IQ app only: an API credential never holds
`automations:approve`.

Needs the `automations:read` scope.

How many approvals are waiting for a decision in your organisation.

Needs the `automations:read` scope.

One approval, with the preview of what its run would change once approved.

Needs the `automations:read` scope.

plan.description: How the workflow would run once kept, as Get import plan answers it. Present for an n8n or Shopify Flow export, where running imported workflows is switched on for your organisation.

canvas.description: The workflow drawn as Get import canvas would draw it once kept. Present when `plan` is.

post.description:
Read an n8n workflow export, a Shopify Flow export, or a workflow described as an intent, and see how Vortex IQ
would run it: the closest templates, and for each step whether it runs, only shows what it would write, or is
not supported. For an export, the answer also carries its `plan` and `canvas` where running imported workflows
is switched on for your organisation. Nothing is saved; [Create import](/automations/api/create-import) keeps
it.

The workflow is checked first: a secret typed into a step is removed and reported. Answers `413` for an export
over the size limit and `422` for one that cannot be read.

Needs the `automations:read` scope.

matches.name: Price and margin exceptions · Shopify
matches.trigger_note: Yours runs daily; this template runs when you press Run by default. You can change it in set-up.

matches.name: Catalogue quality checklist · Shopify
matches.trigger_note: Yours runs daily; this template runs when you press Run by default. You can change it in set-up.

post.description:
Keep an n8n workflow export, a Shopify Flow export, or a described intent, as an import, to set up an
automation from. It is checked and cleaned the same way as [Analyse workflow](/automations/api/analyse-import):
secrets typed into steps are removed, never kept. Nothing runs.

Your organisation keeps up to 100 imports: one more answers `422 allowance_spent`, so delete one you no longer
need first.

Needs the `automations:write` scope.

get.description:
Your organisation's imports, newest first.

Needs the `automations:read` scope.

matches.name: Price and margin exceptions · Shopify
matches.trigger_note: Yours runs daily; this template runs when you press Run by default. You can change it in set-up.

matches.name: Catalogue quality checklist · Shopify
matches.trigger_note: Yours runs daily; this template runs when you press Run by default. You can change it in set-up.

get.description:
One import, read again against the current templates.

Needs the `automations:read` scope.

delete.description:
Delete an import. Automations already set up from it keep running on their own copy.

Needs the `automations:write` scope.

get.description:
How an imported workflow (an n8n or Shopify Flow export) would run as your own automation, step by step:
whether each step runs, only shows what it would write, or is not supported, with the reason, and what a step
needs connected. Nothing runs. Answers `404` for an import made from a description, which has no workflow, and
when running imported workflows is not switched on for your organisation.

Needs the `automations:read` scope.

An imported workflow drawn as n8n draws it (a Shopify Flow export as it runs), for showing it in your own
interface: each step at its position with what Vortex IQ does with it, every connection, and the sticky notes.
Never a step's settings or a credential. Answers `404` as Get import plan does.

Needs the `automations:read` scope.

201.description: Created. State is `active` unless `schedule.cadence` is `manual` (a workflow that starts on a store event takes only that, and is `active`) or a step still needs a connection, then `draft`. Carries `readiness`.

post.description:
Set up an automation that runs an imported workflow (an n8n or Shopify Flow export) as your own, on one of
your [stores](/automations/api/list-stores). The automation keeps its own copy of the workflow, so deleting the
import later changes nothing. A workflow that starts when the store sends an event takes only
`schedule.cadence: manual`, and is `active` at once.

Steps that send somewhere bind to your connections with `bindings` (see
[List destinations](/automations/api/list-destinations)). An automation with a step still unbound is created
as a draft, and stays one until you switch it on: once every step is bound (with
[Update automation](/automations/api/update-automation)), give it its schedule again with Update automation,
or [run it now](/automations/api/run-now); one that starts on a store event, with
[Resume automation](/automations/api/resume-automation). Answers `422` when a step is not supported, a binding
is refused, or running imported workflows is not switched on for your organisation.

Needs the `automations:write` scope.

get.description:
The steps of an automation set up from an imported workflow, as one editable workflow: each step's id, name,
type and settings (with `[removed]` where a secret was), and how the steps connect. Answers `404` for an
automation that is not a workflow.

Needs the `automations:read` scope.

200.description: The differences, and the `preview_hash` to save them with.

409.description: The version read is stale. `data` carries the current automation.

post.description:
What a rewrite of a workflow automation's steps would change, before you save it: the steps added, changed
and removed, and how the new version would run. Nothing is saved. To save it, send the same `workflow` with
the returned `preview_hash` to [Update automation](/automations/api/update-automation).

Needs the `automations:read` scope.

get.description:
A workflow automation drawn as n8n draws it, from its own copy of the workflow, so it still answers after the
import is deleted. Answers `404` for an automation that is not a workflow.

Needs the `automations:read` scope.

Whether Automations are switched on for your organisation. Vortex IQ switches it per organisation; while it is
off, every call made with an API credential's token answers `403`.

Needs the `automations:read` scope.

200.description: Always 200 when the service answers; the state is in the body.

get.description:
How the Automations service is doing right now, as a whole: `state` is `green`, `amber` or `red`, with the
facts behind it (its clock, its capacity, its queue); `connections` alone is your organisation's. Worked out
when you ask; never cached.

Needs the `automations:read` scope.

bearerAuth.description: A bearer token from [Login](/automations/api/login), sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Valid for 60 minutes; it acts as the person named at login, within their organisation, and never approves. Rotating or disabling the organisation's API credential ends every token made with it on its next call. See [Authentication](/automations/api/authentication).

apiCredential.description: Your organisation's API credential, exchanged at [Login](/automations/api/login) for the bearer token above: an OAuth 2.0 client-credentials request, with the `username`, `email` and `organization_name` of the person the token acts as sent as extra fields, as Postman's OAuth 2.0 helper can send them. The token never holds `automations:approve`.

scopes.automations:read: Read automations, templates, stores, runs, the calendar, approvals and imports.
scopes.automations:write: Set automations up, change, pause, resume, archive, restore and run them; move and skip coming runs; keep and delete imports.

Forbidden.description: Your token is valid but may not do this: it lacks the scope, the operation is not part of the Automations API, or Automations are switched off for your organisation.

NotFound.description: Not found. Anything that belongs to another organisation is answered the same way.

TooLarge.description: The body is over its size limit.

TooManyRequests.description: Too many calls in a minute from you or your organisation; nothing was done. `Retry-After` says how many seconds to wait.

Unauthorised.description: The token is missing, has expired, or is no longer valid (for example, the API credential was rotated or disabled). The answer carries `WWW-Authenticate`; log in again for a new token.

Unavailable.description: The service could not complete the request just now. Nothing was changed; try again shortly.

ValidationFailed.description: The request was not valid; `errors` names the fields.

WrongState.description: It is not in a state that allows this; nothing changed.

kind.description: `sends`: a workflow run's collected sends. `checkpoint`: those and a change a later step needs.

request_hash.description: A hash of exactly what will be applied, which the Vortex IQ app sends back when someone decides.

decided_by.description: The id of the person who decided.

ApprovalPreview.description: Exactly what will happen if approved.

content.description: The prepared content (a draft, a list of edits), redacted for display. An object here has whatever keys the program gave it.

changes.description: The named operations, one per object.

ai_read.description: What the AI read, as labels and counts.

ai_review.description: Judgements made by a reviewing skill. Labelled "AI review" on screen, never "measured".

kind.description: `template` runs one of Vortex IQ's templates. `workflow` runs your own imported n8n workflow, and runs only once every step that needs a connection has one.

import_id.description: The import a `workflow` automation was made from; null for a template. The automation keeps its own copy of the plan, so the import may since have been deleted.

source.description: Where a `workflow` automation's workflow came from, `n8n` or `shopify_flow`, kept with the automation so it still answers once the import is deleted. Absent for a template.

bindings.description: A workflow automation's steps bound to your connections; empty for a template.

plan_version.description: The `version` at which a workflow automation's steps or bindings last changed. A run queued on an earlier one is refused as `superseded`.

readiness.description: A `workflow` automation's readiness to be turned on or run now, on the answers about one automation (get, set-up, change). Absent from lists, and for a template.

version.description: Raised on every change. Update automation must carry the version you last read.

platform.description: What it runs on, by kind; null when its template runs on nothing, and it reads `connections` instead.

integration_id.description: The id of the store or account it runs on; null when its template runs on nothing.

store_label.description: The name of what it runs on; for an automation that reads several connections, their names as they were when they were last set.

connections.description:
The connections an automation of a template that runs on nothing reads,
by id and kind, in the order they were set; empty for any other. Part of
its version. Each one's name and state are on `GET /connections`. A
run is refused, naming it, while one of them is not connected. Absent
from an older service.

timezone.description: The timezone its schedule runs in (IANA name).

spread_minutes.description: The fixed offset added to every slot, so "08:00" means "at about 08:00, starts within ten minutes".

send_mode.description: How a workflow automation sends: `ask` (the default) collects a run's sends and waits for approval in the Vortex IQ app; `send` sends at the step.

send_mode_allowed.description: Whether `send_mode: send` would be accepted now (see `send_mode`). On the answers about one `workflow` automation (get and change), as `readiness` is; absent on set-up, where nothing is approved yet, from lists, for a template, and from an older service.

trigger.description: How it starts: on its schedule, or when its store sends an event.

created_by.description: The id of the person who set it up: with this API, the person named at login. Null for one Vortex IQ made itself.

created_via.description: How it was set up: `ui` in the Vortex IQ app, `api-token` through this API. Null for one Vortex IQ made itself.

api_client_id.description: The API credential's client id when `created_via` is `api-token`; null otherwise.

AutomationConnection.description: One connection an automation of a template that runs on nothing reads.

integration_id.description: The store or account it runs on. Required unless its template runs on nothing, and refused when it does.

connections.description:
For a template that runs on nothing, the connections it reads, by id, in
the order to read them: each the organisation's own, connected, and of a
kind in the template's `connections`. Refused for any other template.

timezone.description: The timezone its schedule runs in (IANA name, such as Europe/London); the store's when absent.

platform.description: The store platform the import's steps are for; null when they name none.

store_change_count.description: How many of its steps would change your store; zero means it only reads.

timezone.description: The timezone its schedule runs in (IANA name); its coming runs are worked out again.

bindings.description: A workflow automation's whole map of bound steps; a step left out is unbound. Each binding must be one of your organisation's connections, of the step's kind.

connections.description: The whole list of connections an automation of a template that runs on nothing reads, by id, checked as on set-up; refused for any other.

send_mode.description: A workflow automation's sending, as `Automation.send_mode`. `send` is refused unless `Automation.send_mode_allowed`.

workflow.description: A whole rewrite of a workflow automation's steps, saved as its next version. Sent with `version` and `preview_hash` only.

preview_hash.description: The `preview_hash` from Preview workflow change. The change is saved only when it matches (`preview_mismatch` otherwise).

AutomationTrigger.description: How the automation starts: `schedule`, on its schedule; or `event`, when its store sends one of `topics`.

listening.description: `yes` when the store's subscription for every topic is in place; `not_yet` while it is being made; `failed` with `reason`; `off` while the automation is not active, whether or not another automation keeps the subscription.

reason.description: Why it is not listening, in plain words, when `listening` is `failed`; null otherwise.

events_dropped.description: How many store events were not run: each is a run of this automation that never started, refused as `too_many_waiting` (200 of its runs were already waiting) or `event_too_large` (the event was over 256 KB).

Cadence.description: How often an automation runs. `once` runs on one date and time and then has no next run.

input.description: The destination input's index (n8n's `index`): which input of a Merge it feeds.

type.description: n8n's connection type: main, or a sub-node's such as ai_tool.

CanvasNode.description: One n8n node as the canvas draws it. Never its parameters.

reason.description: The plan's reason, as ImportPlanStep has it.

outputs.description: One entry per output, its label (a Switch's renamed output, true and false, Success and Error, done and loop), or null. At most 5,000: a count written into the export above that is cut there, and a connection can only use an output below it.

inputs.description: How many main inputs it has: 0 for a trigger, 2 or more for a Merge. At most 5,000, as outputs.

subtitle.description: A short description of the step in Vortex IQ's words; never an address or a secret.

text.description: The note's markdown as its author wrote it, after the import's secret check: a note that held a key or a private webhook reads [removed]. Other links and addresses stay, as text.

ConnectionKind.description: One kind of connection, as templates use it.

role.description: `store`: what an automation runs on (a store, or an account such as a cloud account). `account`: a connection a template reads beside its store, such as an advertising account.

noun.description: What a connection of this kind is called: `store` or `account`.

ConnectionPlatform.description: What a connection is for, by connector id: a store (`shopify`, `bigcommerce`), or an account a template reads beside its store (`google_ads`, `klaviyo`, ...).

ContractVersion.description: The version of the API this answer follows. It changes only for a breaking change.

Destination.description: A Google Sheets or Microsoft Teams connection a workflow step can send to. Never a key, and never a Teams address's path or query.

spreadsheet_id.description: The one spreadsheet a service-account Google Sheets connection writes to; null for a Google sign-in, which can reach any spreadsheet you bind, and for Teams.

host.description: Where a Teams connection points: its host only. Null for Google Sheets.

message.description: Plain words saying what happened and what to do.

code.description: A stable code to act on, such as `wrong_state`, `stale_version` or `allowance_spent`.

Health.description: Worked out from live facts when asked. Never cached.

last_tick_at.description: When the schedule clock last ran; null before its first run.

clock.description: When the schedule clock last ran.

seen.description: How many of the workers that run automations have checked in during the last two minutes.

runners.description: Capacity to run automations: the `places` to run in, and how many are `working`.

queue.description: Runs `waiting` to start, and how long the oldest has waited, in seconds.

connections.description: Your organisation's connected stores and accounts.

last_handed_over_at.description: When Vortex IQ last received one of them, as it was made or changed in the Vortex IQ app; null when none has arrived.

steps_source.description: `unavailable` when run step history cannot be read right now (runs carry on either way); otherwise the name of its source.

excluded.description: What was left out of the kept copy, e.g. n8n credential references.

source.description: Where the workflow came from: `n8n` or `shopify_flow`.

platform.description: The store the plan reads; null when the workflow names none (then it cannot run).

plan_hash.description: sha256 of the plan's canonical JSON.

runnable.description: False while any step is not supported, or when the whole workflow is refused (`refusal`); such an import cannot be set up.

refusal.description: Why the whole workflow cannot run (n8n's v0 execution order, no store named), in plain words.

kind.description: How the workflow starts. `event`: when the store sends an event; it takes no schedule and cannot be run by hand.

topic.description: Present exactly when `kind` is `event`: the store event it starts on, as the platform's webhooks name it, such as `inventory_levels/update`.

words.description: Present exactly when `kind` is `event`: that topic in plain words, such as "Runs when stock changes".

schedule.description: The workflow's own schedule, when it can run exactly as written; null when it has none, and you choose one.

trigger_rule.description: The start's Schedule Trigger rule in words, as n8n runs it, with n8n's defaults for what the export leaves out (hour and minute 0, Sunday, day 1): "every weekday at 08:00". Never a URL. Null for a Manual Trigger, a store event (its words are in `trigger.words`), or no start.

trigger_timezone.description: The workflow's own timezone when the export names a real one (`settings.timezone`), as its canonical name (europe/london reads Europe/London); null when it names none, says DEFAULT, or names something that is not a zone.

sends.description: Steps that send through a bound connection (disposition `send`).

reason.description: Plain words: what it would write to, or why it is not supported.

needs.description: What the step needs to run; null when it needs nothing or cannot run.

ImportSource.description: An n8n workflow export, a Shopify Flow export, or an intent already built from a description. Nothing else.

flow.description: A Shopify Flow export as JSON: the exported text without the 64-character prefix and the colon before the JSON.

name.description: What you call it; its words help find the closest template.

ImportTrigger.description: When the workflow runs. A schedule is in the store's time zone; an event is a store event, a webhook or a form.

day.description: Weekly: 1 (Monday) to 7 (Sunday). Monthly: the day of the month.

kind.description: The kind of value. `condition`: an n8n If conditions object, `{ options, conditions: [...], combinator }`, over the field's `fields`, with 1 to 10 conditions; `default` is the condition a new automation starts with.

fields.description: For a `condition`, the fields a rule may compare, read in each run. Absent for every other kind.

default.description: Used when you leave it empty.

max.description: For a number, the largest value; for a list, the most values it takes.

format.description:
What each value must be, beyond its kind: `email`, an email address
(a list of them for a `list`); `integer`, a whole number (for a
`number`: a day of the month, a count). The service refuses a value
that is not one, naming it, so a merchant learns at set-up and not
from a failed run. Absent or null: any text, any number.

mapping.description: How the step was recognised: exact (a catalogue operation), alias (its connector and resource by name), none (not supported yet).

KindNoun.description: `store` for a store's platform; `account` for anything else, such as a cloud account.

Lane.description: `interactive` for a run started by hand, which starts ahead of scheduled work; `scheduled` for the rest.

Occurrence.description: One coming run. `slot_at` is the time the schedule produced and never changes; `run_at` is when it will really run.

automation_version.description: The automation's `version` when this was read, which a move sends back.

timezone.description: The automation's IANA zone, to show the times in.

run_status.description: The run's status once the slot was queued, so a past block can say what happened; null before.

moved_from.description: Where the run was before a person moved it; null when never moved.

version.description: Raised by every edit; 0 for a projected row.

projected.description: Worked out from the schedule further ahead. A move writes it first (send `occurrence_version: 0`); it cannot be skipped until it comes closer.

occurrence_version.description: The coming run's `version` you last read; 0 for a projected one.

Platform.description: What an automation runs on: a store's platform (`shopify`, `bigcommerce`), or an account a template runs on, such as a cloud account (`aws`).

Readiness.description: Whether your organisation can set the template up right now; for a workflow automation, whether it can be turned on or run now.

unconfigured.description: A workflow automation's steps still without a connection they can use, in order. Absent for a template.

missing.description: Connections not present, by kind, always a subset of the template's `connections`; never a key of Vortex IQ's own. Empty when ready.

ReasonCode.description: Why a run did not succeed, as a stable code; `message` says the same in plain words, and what to do. On Vortex IQ's side, setting `platform_fault` and never counting against the automation: `runner_lost`, `service_restart`, `runner_out_of_memory`, `run_over_memory`, `credentials_unavailable`, `needs_review` and `model_unavailable`. The automation's own: `timed_out` and `program_failed`. Neither a failure nor a fault: `connection_missing` (connect what it names), `approval_mismatch`, `refused_check`, `cancelled_by_merchant`, `approval_expired`, `superseded` (the workflow changed after the run was queued), `store_busy` (the store stayed too busy to answer), `automation_off` (the automation was paused, archived or deleted first), and, for a store event that was not run, `too_many_waiting` (200 of its runs were already waiting) and `event_too_large` (the event was over 256 KB).

Receipt.description: What the run read, and which AI model it used, if any.

ResultView.description: How a template's runs read as a table: which list in the run's `result` holds the rows, which fields are columns, and which are offered as filters.

version.description: The view's own format version; 1 for every packaged template.

title.description: The table's heading, for example `Stock review`.

description.description: What to do with the rows, in a sentence.

collection.description: The key in the run's `result` whose array holds the rows; `records` for every packaged template.

columns.description: The row fields shown as columns, in order.

filters.description: The row fields offered as filters. Not every one is a column, and a row need not carry every one.

page_size.description: Rows per page; 25 for every packaged template.

event_ref.description: For a run a store event started: the topic and what it was about, such as `inventory_levels/update · 4471`; never the event's body. Null otherwise.

message.description: Plain words for you, including what to do next.

platform_fault.description: True when the run ended because of a fault on Vortex IQ's side; it then never counts against the automation.

queue_wait_ms.description: Time from queued to started, in milliseconds.

summary.description: One or two sentences of what was found or done.

result.description: The program's result, redacted, capped at 256 KB. Its shape is the template's `result_view`; for a `workflow` automation it is a `WorkflowResult`.

result_truncated.description: True when the result was too large to include in full.

created_by.description: The id of the person who started it by hand: with this API, the person named at login. Null for a run its schedule or a store event started.

created_via.description: How it was started: `ui` in the Vortex IQ app, `api-token` through this API. Null for a run its schedule or a store event started.

api_client_id.description: The API credential's client id when `created_via` is `api-token`; null otherwise.

idempotency_key.description: A key you make, at least 8 characters, new for each run you mean, and one across all your organisation's automations: the same key returns the same run, and one already used for another automation is refused.

RunMode.description: `normal`, or `test`: reads are real and every change to your store is refused.

RunTrigger.description: How the run started: `manual` (by hand), `schedule`, or `event` (a store event). `retry` is reserved and not used yet.

RunUsage.description: What the run used, measured, never estimated.

run_at.description: The time of day in the automation's timezone, `HH:MM`. Required for once, daily, weekdays, weekly and monthly.

day_of_week.description: 1 is Monday. Required for weekly, and for monthly with `week_of_month`.

day_of_month.description: For monthly, unless `week_of_month` is given. 31 runs on the last day of a shorter month.

date.description: Required for once; the local calendar day it runs on, in the automation's timezone. A day and time already passed are refused.

days.description: For weekdays; which days, 1 is Monday. Absent means Monday to Friday.

week_of_month.description: For monthly, with `day_of_week`; the first to fourth, or -1 the last, such weekday of the month, instead of `day_of_month`.

timezone.description: An IANA zone name, such as Europe/London.

StaleAutomation.description: A refusal that carries the current automation, so you can read it again and retry.

StaleOccurrence.description: A refusal that carries the current coming run, so you can read it again and retry.

Step.description: One step of a run: a call to a connector or a skill, as labels and counts only (no payloads, nothing personal).

reused.description: True when a cached answer was reused instead of a new call.

count.description: Records read or written by this step, when known.

integration_id.description: The id of one of your organisation's connections (see List destinations).

kind.description: The kind of connection, never `store`: the store is the automation's own.

target.description: For a Google sign-in Sheets connection, the spreadsheet (and tab) the step writes to, which it may reach; a service-account connection is one spreadsheet already. Null for the other kinds.

StepBindings.description: A workflow automation's steps bound to connections, by the n8n step's name (unique in a workflow).

StepDisposition.description: `run`: runs in Vortex IQ. `send`: writes through the connection bound to the step. `unsupported`: cannot run in this version.

StepNeedKind.description: What a step needs to run: `store`, the automation's own store, always there; or a Google Sheets or Microsoft Teams connection you bind.

StepTarget.description: Where a step's connection must lead, as far as the plan can read it from the step. A field the step decides only while running is null or absent.

spreadsheet_id.description: The spreadsheet a Google Sheets step writes to or reads.

Store.description: What an automation can run on: a store, or an account a template runs on, such as a cloud account. Never its keys.

integration_id.description: The id of the store or account, which you pass as `integration_id` when you create an automation.

timezone.description: The timezone (IANA name) a new automation on this store runs in unless you choose another.

state.description: `connected`, or `disconnected`: a disconnected store is listed so you can see why an automation on it cannot run, and is never one to set a new automation up on.

handed_over_at.description: When Vortex IQ last received this store's connection, as it was made or changed in the Vortex IQ app.

platform.description: What the template runs on, by kind; null for a template that runs on no single store or account, which reads the connections you choose instead.

trigger.description: How an automation of this template starts when it is not on a schedule, such as when stock changes; null for a scheduled template.

steps.description: The template's steps in run order, in plain words.

sentence.description: The one-line read-back shown on set-up, in plain words.

connections.description: The connections the template needs, by kind: its store's platform first, then every other connection its steps use, in step order.

reads.description: What it reads, each with a sensitivity tier.

tier.description: How sensitive what it reads is. `marketing` is an advertising or email account; `public` is a page anyone can open, such as a page-speed test.

writes.description: Named operations it may perform after approval. Empty means it only reads.

weight.description: `ordinary` or `heavy`: how demanding a run of this template is.

result_view.description: How the records in a run's `result` read as a table: which fields are columns and which are filters.

records_called.description: What the records in a run's `result.records` are called, in the plural, such as "findings".

kinds.description: Every kind of connection, with its display name.

TemplateStep.description: One step of a template, in plain words.

kind.description: What the step does, in one word: Reads, Checks, Writes, Gives you, AI prepares, or You.

note.description: What the step does, in a sentence. May be empty.

connector.description: The connector the step calls, by id, or null for a step that calls none.

paged.description: True when the call sits inside a loop and reads page after page.

on_fail.description: What happens if the step cannot finish, when the program says.

gives.description: The fields the step hands back.

inputs.description: The values written into the step, by name.

topics.description: The platform's own topic strings, as its webhooks name them: `inventory_levels/update`, `store/sku/inventory/updated`.

words.description: When it runs, in plain words: "Runs when stock changes".

why.description: `no_connection`: none bound, or the bound one is not yours or not of the step's kind. `wrong_target`: it leads to another spreadsheet. `needs_reconnecting`: the connection is disconnected; connect it again in the Vortex IQ app. `not_arrived` is reserved and not used yet.

integration_id.description: The id of the store it reads (see List stores).

schedule.description: A workflow that starts on a store event (`ImportPlan.trigger.kind` `event`) takes only `{ "cadence": "manual" }`: it has no timetable.

timezone.description: The timezone its schedule runs in (IANA name); the store's when absent.

bindings.description: Steps bound to your connections at set-up. A step left unbound keeps the automation off, as a draft.

WorkflowCanvas.description: An imported workflow drawn as n8n draws it. Never a step's settings, a credential or a removed secret.

bounds.description: Every node's box (its tile and the label beneath) and every note, for fit-to-view.

trigger.description: Where runs start, as the plan chose it; null when the workflow has no start Vortex IQ runs.

rule.description: The start in words: a Schedule Trigger's rule, or for a store event what starts it, such as "Runs when stock changes". Null for a Manual Trigger.

timezone_origin.description: An automation's read only, where its timezone came from; null for an import, and for an automation set up before it was kept.

source.description: Where the workflow came from, as the import's plan says it; an automation's canvas is always n8n's, the only kind that becomes one.

WorkflowChange.description: One difference a rewrite makes. `before` and `after` are whole.

step.description: The step's name after the change; for a removed step, its name before.

path.description: For `value`: a step field (`disabled`, `type_version`) or a parameter path (`sheetName.value`, `assignments.assignments[0].value`).

bindings.description: Connections to change, by step name, over the bindings carried from the current version (a renamed step keeps its own; a removed step's go with it).

WorkflowEditNode.description: One step, as Get workflow reads it and Preview workflow change takes it back. No position and no credentials.

id.description: The step's id from the read; absent for a new step, which is given one.

disabled.description: Left out, an existing step keeps its own; a new step is on.

preview_hash.description: sha256 of the canonical JSON of the version previewed against, the new plan and its bindings.

unconfigured.description: Every step that would still need a connection once saved.

notices.description: Each value of the rewrite that looked like a key and was left out, by step and field, saying to connect it instead; never the value. A rewrite that moves the start to or from a store event says so here too.

version.description: The automation's version the workflow was read at.

needs.description: Each step's need, by step name, as the plan has it.
